To solve that problem, this article proposes a high-speed detection method to measure the peak voltage of the periodic electromagnetic disturbance inside the chip. The circuit contains a synchronizer to align the sampling time to the peak time. A dynamic comparator is employed to compare the actual voltage of the disturbance peak with its “guessed” value. The comparison result switches capacitors in a capacitor digital-to-analog convertor (CDAC) and let its output voltage gradually approaches the disturbance peak voltage. The proposed peak detector is implemented using TSMC 0.18 µm CMOS process. It has a small area of 0.737 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, The post-layout simulation show that the detector can accurately measure the peak voltage of the disturbance signals with amplitudes ranging from 0.1 V to 0.8 V and frequencies up to 1.1GHz. For all process corner conditions, the measured voltage is difference from the actual value for less than 1%. The detector has the advantages of high detection accuracy, width frequency range, and small area occupation. The work presented in this article provide a new solution for the circuit design in the on-chip EMI Test.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Ultra-Low-Cost Impedance Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: A novel impedance analyzer working in the range of 500 Hz to 500 kHz is proposed in this paper. Based on the proposed Wave Adder circuit, Peak Detector circuit, and Multilayer Perceptron algorithm, the designed analyzer can measure the impedance value of an object without any high-speed ADCs (Analog-to-digital Converters) or proprietary impedance measuring chips. Besides, the proposed hardware can achieve extremely low production costs (less than ¥35) while still obtaining reliable impedance analyzer functionality. In order to validate the proposed analyzer, a demonstration system was presented in this paper, with an upper machine (Android APP) and a lower machine (ESP32 Based analyzer). The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed analyzer could reach a 5% measurement error in the frequency range of 500 Hz to 500 kHz, which might be a promising solution for designs of low-cost impedance analyzers.

articleTitle: A Fast Spectral Analysis Method Based on Sparse Signals in Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In the oscilloscope for electronic testing, the traditional fast Fourier transform (FFT) faces problems such as high computational complexity, low frequency resolution, and unsuitability for sparse signals. To solve these problems, we propose a spectrum analysis method based on sparse Fourier transform (SFT). SFT is a new algorithm that uses the characteristics of the signal itself to obtain the signal spectrum, which is more efficient than the traditional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{FFT}^{\underline{12}}$</tex>. The main steps of SFT include spectrum rearrangement, filtering, subsampled FFT, localization and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{evaluation}^{\underline{13}}$</tex>. We use the theoretical framework of SFT to design a spectrum analysis method suitable for oscilloscopes, breaking through the limitations of the spectrum analysis function on the number of operation points in the existing system, and greatly improving the efficiency in sparse signal testing. We verify the effectiveness and superiority of our method through experiments and look forward to its application prospects in the field of electronic testing.

articleTitle: Research on Detection and Simulation Method of Electric Data Acquisition Link Based on Fault Injection Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the current test items of China's electric data acquisition and testing laboratory are not in line with the actual use environment. This paper proposes a simulation scheme of electricity information acquisition link based on fault injection technology. Taking the intelligent electric meter as an example, this scheme uses fault injection technology such as signal interference and message tampering to simulate the abnormal working condition information of the field operation, and detects the function, performance and reliability of the intelligent electric meter in this environment. The comprehensive failure rate decreased by 75.64 % in different scenarios. In addition, the research also provides effective data support for the quality evaluation system of electric data acquisition of the intelligent electric meter, which can better meet the needs of electricity information collection in the actual use environment and improve the accuracy and reliability of detection.

articleTitle: Research of Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method Based on BO-DK-ELM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: Aiming at solving the problems that the parameters of the traditional Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) model have significant impact on the fault diagnosis accuracy while it is applied in rolling bearings, a rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on Bayesian Optimization Deep Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (BO-DK-ELM) was proposed in this paper. Firstly, a model based on Deep Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (DK-ELM) algorithm is constructed by combining the Auto Encoder (AE) with the traditional Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (K-ELM); Secondly, the Bayesian Optimization (BO) algorithm is applied to find the optimal hyper-parameters in the above proposed DK-ELM model, in order to minimize the sum of classification error rates of the training and validation sets in the DK-ELM model. And then the testing set would be fed into the trained BO-DK-ELM model for fault diagnosis. Finally, our proposed method was validated using the Case Western Reserve University bearing fault dataset, and the final results show that its fault diagnosis accuracy can reach 99.0%. Meanwhile, compared with other traditional intelligent fault diagnosis algorithms, the proposed method has higher fault diagnosis accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of New Power System User Side Terminal Flexible Interactive Function Detecting System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: Aiming at the problems that the flexible interactive function introduced by the user side terminal in the new power system lacks rapid detection means and the detecting method is quite different from the actual situation, a flexible interactive function detecting scheme is proposed, a detecting system is designed, and relevant experiments are conducted. The results show that the detecting system can detect the flexible interaction function of the user side terminal close to the actual situation, and the overall detecting time is shortened by 35.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> compared with the traditional detection. The development of the detecting system provides a new method for the rapid detection of flexible interactive functions of user side terminals and promotes the large scale application of user side terminals such as energy controllers and smart energy units.

articleTitle: Dynamic Performance Assessment Technique of Satellite Star Sensor Using In-Orbit Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: Star sensor is an important attitude measurement instrument of spacecraft. The dynamic performance is an indicator to assess the ability of star sensor to track the star stably and export the attitude accurately. However, few studies have assessed the in-orbit dynamic performance of star sensor in China presently. This paper analyzed the satellite star sensor in-orbit performance assessment index system, designed the corresponding assessment method, and carried out the assessment and verification based on the actual in-orbit data on the evaluate system of satellite in-orbit data, which shows that the assessment model designed in this paper can effectively assess the in-orbit dynamic performance of star sensors. The study of the evaluation of the star sensor in-orbit performance can also provide idea for the in-orbit performance evaluation of other satellite sensors or actuators, and support the long-term management or the test and evaluation of satellite in orbit.

articleTitle: Fabric Defect Detection Based on FCN Uncertainty Feature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of fabric defect detection based on Full Convolutional neural network (FCN) algorithm, a fabric defect detection method based on FCN uncertain features was proposed. Based on the model features of the stacked denoising automatic encoder, the natural attribute of detection uncertainty is added to the detection system, forming a new hybrid FCN model. The over fitting of the model will cause the performance of the training samples to be too superior, resulting in a large Generalization error of the model. In order to prevent the FCN over fitting phenomenon and improve the detection efficiency of the network in the network training process, this paper introduces Dropout in the full connection layer, and temporarily discards the neural network unit from the network according to a certain probability. Image artifacts seriously affect the quality of images. A new hybrid downsampling method is proposed to reduce image artifacts caused by the convolution process through deconvolution algorithms. Experiments have shown that this algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of FCN foreign object detection, and the PR curve of the algorithm is superior to existing algorithms, which can achieve effective detection of fabric defects.

articleTitle: Passive Piston Gas Flow Standard Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: Piston gas flow standard device can be divided into passive piston gas flow standard device and active piston gas flow standard device. In order to measure the micro gas flow, a passive piston gas flow standard device was developed, which can verify or calibrate the thermal gas mass flowmeter, gas laminar flow sensor, gas volumetric flowmeter and float flowmeter with the flow range of (0.02∼20) L/min under the pressure of (0.1∼0.6) MPa. The relative expanded uncertainty of the master standard of the standard device is 0.16% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(k=2)$</tex>. The thermal gas mass flowmeter with good stability and repeatability was selected to test on this standard device, with the flow point 100 mL/min. The uncertainty of the test results is evaluated, and the relative expanded uncertainty of the measurement result is 0.17% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(k=2)$</tex>. It is proved that the standard device can measure the small gas flow, and has a small relative expanded uncertainty, which means the accuracy level of the standard device is high.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Telemetry Simulation Equipment for Target Missile
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In order to realize the simulation of the transmission of telemetry data during the flight process of the target missile and the interpretation of the data by the receiving end, this paper designs and implements an telemetry simulation device based on FPGA and MCU controller, and develops the supporting application software. The joint test results with the ground telemetry signal receiving system show that the device can send multiple sets of simulated telemetry data in real time, and realize the real-time send-transmission-reception link of telemetry together with the ground telemetry system. Also the equipment can be used to verify the technical status of the ground telemetry in routine inspections, or replace the telemetry equipment on the missile and carry out technical docking with the ground telemetry system, has good portability and operability, and can be applied to the daily operation training of the telemetry system.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv7 Fusion Detection Line for Swimming Pool Drowning Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In order to ensure the safety of swimmers, an improved method for preventing drowning in video surveillance is proposed by integrating a region-based timing detection line into the YOLOv7 algorithm. The utilization of the region-based timing detection line enables preliminary assessment of swimmer behaviors, thereby reducing the rate of false drowning detections. To enhance the extraction of swimmer behavior features, the YOLOv7 algorithm incorporates the DCNv3 (Deformable Convolutional Network) module. Additionally, a Wise-IoU dynamic focal boundary box regression loss function based on attention is employed to decrease the rate of missed detections and enhance the overall detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the region-based timing detection line can accurately detect swimmers. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm exhibits a 3.6% improvement in recall rate and a 2.9% increase in average precision when compared to the YOLOv7 algorithm. Notably, it demonstrates superior performance in detecting behaviors of swimmers who are obstructed or located at a distance.

articleTitle: An Analysis on Effects of Different Input Phases and Amplitudes on Power Combining
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In this paper, effects of different input signal phases and amplitudes on the output are analyzed when the Wilkinson combiner is used for power combining. According to the circuit theory and the transmission line model of the combiner, the relationships between the power received by the load port and that dissipated in the shunt resistor are deduced when two input signals have a phase or amplitude difference. Moreover, two special cases where two input signals are equal in amplitude or phase are discussed. Relevant demonstration circuits are created with GaAs chips by wire bonding to verify such cases. The proposed results can be helpful to the engineering application of power combining and phased array synthesis.

articleTitle: Application of Image Mosaic in Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that industrial endoscope cannot detect accurately due to the limited field of vision caused by the internal structure of the machine, a defect detection method based on image processing is proposed. In this paper, an adaptive double threshold image mosaic algorithm based on SIFT is designed. Firstly, the normalized histogram method is used for threshold segmentation of defect samples to reduce the computational complexity of building a gaussian difference pyramid. Then, by setting the accuracy of matching feature points to meet the requirements, the threshold will be adjusted to a more reasonable range. Finally, a reasonable data model is estimated iteratively by RANSAC algorithm. By this way, the wrong matching points that do not fit the model will be removed. The experimental results show that the speed of the improved algorithm is increased by 41.72% compared with the traditional algorithm. The relative error of defect measurement can reach 0.59%. The proposed method has high measuring accuracy and can be widely used in the internal defect detection of machines.

articleTitle: Method for Delay Recovery of Trigger Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: This article presents a method of utilizing the SPARTAN-6 series Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) to precisely measure the arrival time of trigger signals and subsequently recover them based on a predefined delay. In various nodes of the accelerator, it's necessary to delay the output of received trigger signals. To obtain an accurate recovery signal, we employ the carry chain within the FPGA to precisely measure the arrival time of the trigger signals. Simultaneously, we use the carry chain to accurately control the output delay. Ultimately, we generate a recovery signal with a time resolution of less than 120 ps.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of GPU-Based Frequency Domain Analysis Function in the Digital Oscilloscope
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of digital signals, the digital oscilloscope which only has the time domain analysis function has been unable to meet the user's needs. In the traditional digital storage oscilloscopes, the frequency domain analysis module is based on the FFT algorithm, and it runs on the CPU in a serial manner. In this paper, we propose a frequency domain analysis framework based on OpenGL technology, which significantly increases the analysis speed of signals while reducing CPU occupancy and memory consumption. the CPU is responsible for the overall scheduling and data flow control, and each sub-module of frequency analysis function runs in the GPU in parallel, and data transfer between CPU and GPU is minimized. The experimental results show that the time consumption and memory consumption of the new architecture is more advantageous when using data volumes over 16k for analysis, and the optimization improves significantly as the data volume increases; when using 128M data volumes for analysis, the total time consumption is only 1/10 of that under the original CPU framework, and the time actually spent on computation is only 1/33 of the original time consumption.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Completely Centered Integrated 3D Cutting Force Sensor Based on Decagonal Ring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: The cutting forces during cutting can visually reflect various conditions of the cutting process, such as tool wear and workpiece machining. Based on the decagonal ring, a fully aligned integrated cutting force sensor is designed, and a calibration collet is designed for the calibration of the 3D force, and the sensor is encapsulated. The sensor and the calibration collet are calibrated by finite element software, and the first six orders of inherent frequencies and modal vibration patterns are calculated by modal analysis. Full-scale loading of the sensor in three directions for several times, found that the sensor initial output did not change, indicating that the sensor design meets the strength requirements.

articleTitle: Design of Self-Calibration Based High Resolution Frequency Measurement Module
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: This paper proposes a self-calibration based high resolution frequency measurement method. Based on the analog interpolation technique of time-to-amplitude conversion, the measurement of two ways standard time interval is added to reduce the error introduced by temperature change and voltage drift. The measurement data are processed using the least square method to diminish random errors. Test results show that the frequency measurement resolution reaches 12 bits/s and the measurement accuracy is better than ±0.02ppm. Compared with classic measurement techniques, the proposed approach has a broad application prospect as it improves frequency measurement resolution and measurement accuracy with lower cost and convenient calibration.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Heading Estimation Based on F-LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: When global navigation satellite system navigation signals are restricted or unavailable, using the inertial measurement unit and magnetometer of a smartphone for pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR) is a simple and highly practical navigation positioning solution. Since heading estimation is the main source of error in PDR positioning, this paper proposes a correction scheme based on the Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to solve the problem of heading angle estimation errors when using a smartphone for PDR. The proposed F-LSTM (Fully Connected LSTM) network is trained on data collected in various heading directions to regressively approximate the non-linear sensor error. The data collection is relatively small, and the training time is short, which improves the practicality of the model. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of heading angle estimation, with the heading estimation error less than 4°. The algorithm is integrated with classical PDR. The positioning error that is less than 2.44 % of the total distance.

articleTitle: GA-PNN Based Multi-Gas Sensor Temperature Modulation Mode Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: The temperature modulation technique based on semiconductor gas sensors is a kind of multi-modal characteristic signal output with temperature dependence by periodically changing the heating temperature mode of the sensor, which can effectively address the low response rate and poor selectivity issues encountered in semiconductor gas sensors. To improve the detection characteristics of the sensor for four environmental test gases, CH4, CO, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>OH, and NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, this paper uses rectangular wave temperature modulation mode for low-frequency dynamic performance test analysis, discrete wavelet transform and principal component analysis for dynamic information feature extraction and dimensionality reduction, combined with GA-PNN model for optimal identification. The results show that the selectivity of gas detection is improved in all the nine designed temperature modulation modes, and the response rate is improved significantly. Among them, the gas qualitative analysis accuracy can reach 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in the rectangular wave modulation mode with 4–5 V bias and a 20 s period, opening up a new semiconductor sensor detection path.

articleTitle: Microscopic Modelling for EMAT in Ferromagnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: There are three main mechanisms in the transduction process of ferromagnetic material electromagnetic acoustic transducers (EMAT), Lorentz force, magnetization force, and magnetostriction, among which the modeling of magnetostriction is insufficient. Since the change of the magnetic flux density always lags behind the change of the magnetic field, and the magnetization process is nonlinear, the electromagnetic acoustic transducer cannot be well described. Moreover, the use of high-frequency excitation in the electromagnetic acoustic transducer causes the magnetization process to be dynamic magnetization process, and it cannot be simply approximated via a hysteresis loop. The main work of this paper is to establish an electromagnetic acoustic transducer model suitable for ferromagnetic materials, and to dedicate to describe the nonlinear process of the magnetostriction from a microscopic point of view. On top of this, the dynamic magnetization process is considered under certain conditions. The model was validated by finite element simulations, and the results agreed well with the model.

articleTitle: Design of Inter-Satellite Link Between Multifunction Test Sat and Tiantuo 5
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: By introducing inter-satellite link, Multifunction Test Sat and Tiantuo 5 can realize functions such as cooperative positioning, formation control and distributed computing. In order to reduce the construction and development costs of inter-satellite link, low-cost commercial devices such as the Long Range Radio (Lora) chip from Semtech company are used to achieve inter-satellite communication. Combined with the characteristics of relative motion between two satellites, adaptive algorithms are used to adaptively adjust the parameter configuration of the Lora chip to achieve optimal communication transmission performance. The analysis of the actual in orbit operation data of the Multifunction Test Sat and Tiantuo-5 satellite shows that the communication rate using Lora chip reaches 126.88bps. The design and development of the inter-satellite link proposed in this article is simple, small in size, low in energy consumption, and high in sensitivity; At the same time, it is possible to adaptively configure communication encoding and communication rate based on the actual operation of dual satellites, effectively improving the utilization rate of onboard energy and saving onboard energy.

articleTitle: DAACN: Dense Atrous Asymmetric Convolutional Network for HIFU Treatment Target Region Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In the context of HIFU treatment monitoring for ultrasonic image segmentation, there is a trade-off between the segmentation accuracy and the complexity of semantic segmentation methods. High-accuracy methods tend to be computationally complex, while low-complexity methods are prone to missegmentation issues related to the shape and boundary of the treatment target region. To address this challenge., this paper proposes a novel approach called Dense Atrous Asymmetric Convolutional Network (DAACN). DAACN is a lightweight network with an encoder-decoder architecture that incorporates non-symmetric convolutions and dense atrous convolutions. It achieves efficient extraction of image features while maintaining a low computational complexity. Additionally, this study proposes the use of multi-cross-entropy loss to supervise the network and preserve more details and contextual information during the training process, thereby further improving the accuracy of the segmentation. The experimental results demonstrate that the DAACN trained with the multi-cross-entropy loss function achieved a parameter count of 3.22M. Compared to other networks, it exhibits excellent segmentation accuracy, with MIoU and DSC values of 95.07% and 97.47% respectively.

articleTitle: A Method of Ferromagnetic Object Identification Based on Magnetic Sensor and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: Magnetic sensor is a magnetic inductance sensor, which has the advantages of high sensitivity, wide measurement range, and low energy consumption compared to other magnetic field sensors, such as magnetic gate sensors and magnetic inductance sensors. Magnetic sensors are widely used in various domains such as metal detection, safety inspection, and drone navigation. This paper describes a ferromagnetic Object detection method based on magnetic sensor. This method uses a magnetic sensor to obtain the changes in spatial magnetic field intensity caused by the continuous movement of the measured object over a certain distance within the magnetic field range, thereby identifying the type of object. The principle of this method is to carry out feature extraction, parameter training and Generative model generation for the data of varying magnetic field intensity generated by the continuous movement of various ferromagnetic objects to be measured through machine learning algorithm in advance, so as to realize Object detection. The three-axis data obtained by sensors need to be preprocessed through three steps: step 1 data filtering. Step 2 is data processing. and step 3 is data fusion before it can be used for machine learning. In the process of machine learning, this article horizontally compares three mainstream learning algorithms: SVM(Support Vector Machine), RandomForest, and LightGBM(Light Gradient Boosting Machine), all of which can achieve high recognition rates. Finally, two sets of experiments verify that this method can be applied to the identification of multiple ferromagnetic Object detection with different shapes and different ferromagnetic individuals with the same shape.

articleTitle: Study on the Key Parameters of Flow Element for Particle Samplers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In view of the deficiency of flow orifice flow element commonly used in particle samplers, we began to develop an orifice flow element with a small gas flow range. The inlet Reynolds number of the corresponding flow element in this flow range does not exceed two thousand, basically belonging to the laminar flow state, which has exceeded the application range of the differential pressure flow element specified by the existing various standards. In order to ensure the flow performance of the newly designed orifice, it is necessary to give the maximum allowable deviation of the three key parameters of orifice thickness E, throttle orifice thickness e and pressure extraction position. Computational fluid dynamics simulation was used to determine the maximum allowable deviation of the parametric machining of the above geometric dimensions. For two kinds of microflow orifice plates with different flow rates, the recommended thickness of the microflow orifice plate and the recommended thickness of the throttle orifice, and the corresponding maximum allowable geometric deviation were obtained. The upper and lower reaches used D-D/2 pressure, the accuracy of the upstream pressure position was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.1\mathrm{D}$</tex>, and the accuracy of the downstream pressure position was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.05\mathrm{D}$</tex>. Based on this key dimension, the linearity of the outflow coefficient and the processing consistency of the designed laminar flow orifice are better than 1.5 per cent.

articleTitle: Element Defective Sample Augmentation Method Based on Improved DCGAN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: The deep learning-based methods for inspecting defects of printing label are usually having problems such as difficult to collect training samples and insufficient training accuracy. In this paper, a defect sample augmentation method based on improved DCGAN network is proposed to achieve effective augmentation of a limited sample dataset, where spectral normalization and Wasserstein distance are introduced into the original DCGAN network. The generated defective sample by the original DCGAN and the improved network are compared, and the generalization of the proposed method is verified by applied to augment the sample images of different element in printing label. The influence of image resolution and defect size of the original samples on the network training are investigated respectively. The experimental results show that the improved DCGAN could effectively alleviate the phenomenon of pattern collapse and gradient vanishing that existed in the original network during the training process, and the morphology and location of defects in the generated defect samples are diversity and randomness.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis Method of Measurement Uncertainty and Application in Pitot-Wind Tunnel Standard Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: This study explores a dynamic analysis method for evaluating measurement uncertainty in the measurement process by calculating the distribution of measurement uncertainty at multiple measurement points within the measurement range. The analysis method provides an intuitive and visual representation of the measurement uncertainty, given a mathematical model and equipment configuration. A wind tunnel device with a Pitot tube as a standard was used to analyze the uncertainty of the flow velocity measurement. The dynamic analysis method was applied to assess the uncertainty of the measurement results and compare the measurement uncertainty of different differential pressure transmitters with various measuring ranges. The transmitter configuration was optimized to improve the measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: Water Stress Analysis of Strawberry Based on Color Space Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: In order to investigate the effect of water stress on strawberry seedlings, a chlorophyll fluorescence acquisition system was built based on chlorophyll fluorescence imaging technology. By conducting grouped water stress incubation experiments on strawberry seedlings, the water content and chlorophyll content (SPAD) of leaves were measured at the same moment for 14 consecutive days, and the RGB, HSV and HSI color space models of true color images were converted using MATLAB software based on the collected chlorophyll fluorescence images. The experimental results showed that the leaf water content of the experimental group decreased with the increase of chlorophyll content and the correlation coefficient of the correlation model is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.96$</tex>; When channel components in color space were used to characterize the water stress condition of strawberry seedlings, the correlation between the water content of the leaves of experimental group B and the channel component I was the highest, with a modeled correlation coefficient of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.88$</tex>; the correlation between the chlorophyll content (SPAD) of the leaves of experimental group B and the channel component I was the highest, with a modeled correlation coefficient of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.89$</tex>. The average relative error between the validation and prediction groups did not exceed 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> when the water content and chlorophyll content of seedling leaves under water stress were predicted using I-channel components. In summary, the I-channel of HSI color space model can be used to characterize the water content and chlorophyll content (SPAD) of strawberry seedling leaves under water stress, thus effectively conducting the assessment of plant stress status and providing some reference value for agricultural development.

articleTitle: Study on the Capacity Measurement Method of Large LNG Film Tanks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: As a new type of storage tank for LNG, large LNG film tanks have been built on a large scale in China in recent years. The two 220,000 m3 film tanks built in Nangang Industrial Zone of Tianjin Economic Development Zone are the first LNG film tanks built in China and the largest in the world on land. However, due to the complex internal structure, huge volume and ultra-low temperature working condition of LNG storage tanks, the accuracy of their capacity measurement is difficult to be effectively guaranteed. This paper introduces two methods for capacity measurement of large LNG thin-film tanks according to their structural characteristics, solving the problem of precision measurement of thin-film structures in large space dimensions. The research results surface that the methods can achieve fast and accurate volume measurement of thin-film tanks, which has important guiding significance for capacity measurement of LNG thin-film tanks.

articleTitle: An Adaptive DenseNet-Based Method with Knowledge Distillation for Lightweight Infrared and Visible Sensors Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: Current infrared and visible image fusion technologies based on deep learning mainly improve the quality and statistical indicators of fused images by increasing model complexity and weight size. To address this issue, we propose a novel dual-light fusion approach using Adaptive DenseN et with knowledge distillation. Our approach leverages pre-existing fusion models to learn and compress while meeting the requirements of model compression through the use of hyperparameters such as the width and depth of the model network. This study evaluates the effectiveness of our proposed approach on a new dataset comprising three public datasets, namely FLIR, M3FD and LLVIP. Through qualitative and quantitative experiments, we demonstrate that the distillated Adaptive DenseNet model, proposed in this study, effectively matches the performance of the original fusion models. Furthermore, when compared to the original models, the models obtained using our method exhibit significant advantages as the average inference time is reduced to 13.47%, and the average model size is reduced to 5.43 % in dual light image fusion.

articleTitle: Virtual Test Technology Based on Digital Twins for Satellite Intelligent Integrated Electronic System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: With the development of satellite autonomy, intelligence, and systematization, the degree of intelligence of onboard integrated electronic system is becoming higher and higher, and its testing complexity and requirements for the ability to build testing scenarios are becoming higher and higher. In response to the shortcomings of low efficiency in traditional physical verification, difficulty in constructing intelligent testing scenarios, and difficulty in verifying boundary conditions, the satellite virtual test technology based on digital twins for intelligent integrated electronic system is studied. The digital twin of the integrated electronic system is achieved through virtual computer technology, running the real satellite operating system and various intelligent apps and collaborating with satellite system models and other satellite models to build a high fidelity virtual test platform for onboard intelligent application software. The virtual test platform adopts standard protocol interfaces to seamlessly connect with satellite ground test system software, conducting test scheduling and satellite-ground data interaction like testing real satellites, simulating various task scenarios, boundary scenarios, and abnormal scenarios, and completing virtual test for onboard integrated electronic system. This can serve as a reference for the development of domestic intelligent satellite virtual test technology.

articleTitle: Improving Infrared Pedestrian Detection by Sharing Visible Light Domain Information with Enhanced UNet and YOLO Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: The development of effective pedestrian detection approaches is of great importance for ensuring safety in automatic driving and accurate monitoring in low illumination or occlusion conditions. However, the detection task is complicated due to the absence of clear visual cues and the presence of background noise in infrared images. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an infrared pedestrian detection approach that utilizes an improved UNet and YOLO network to share visible light information from multiple related datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving high pedestrian detection accuracies in different public infrared pedestrian datasets.

articleTitle: A Digital Oscilloscope Based Hardware Implementation Approach for Universal Memristor Emulators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 16th International Conference on Electronic Measurement & Instruments (ICEMI)
abstract: Prior to nanoscale memristors are commercially viable, accurately verifying the characteristics of memristors in hardware is one of the effective approaches to rapidly expanding their engineering by applications. Nevertheless, the commonly used equivalent circuit based on commercial devices has issues: large errors, inefficiency, and compatibility. This paper proposes a general digital model for memristors based on Taylor expansion and introduces a polynomial order determination method. Numerical simulations confirm that the proposed model exhibits three typical characteristics of memristors. Afterwards, a reconfigurable memristor simulator is developed based on FPGA. Finally, the simulator is embedded in a digital oscilloscope, and an interface is designed to display the hysteresis loop of the memristor. In addition, by online modification of the polynomial coefficients, the existing memristors can be simulated in the designed platform and the phase trajectory can be displayed with high accuracy.
